headline: Record profit, a share split and a bigger dividend
text: On 19 January Schlumberger announced a two-for-one share split and raised its dividend by 19 percent. A day later it reported 2005 net income of 2.21 billion dollars, up 78 percent per share, and record oilfield revenue. Chief executive Andrew Gould expects exploration to 'show a large increase in 2006' and to continue for years, with shortages of people and equipment across the industry.
source: Schlumberger press release of 19 January 2006, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/87347/000119312506008573/dex991.htm (read 2026-10-03); Schlumberger press release of 20 January 2006, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/87347/000119312506008958/dex991.htm (read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: A Schlumberger site at Vechta, Germany, with the company sign

headline: A record 36 billion dollars, and a new boss
text: ExxonMobil reported on 30 January a 2005 profit of 36.13 billion dollars, by far the largest in its history (2004: 25.33 billion), including 10.71 billion in the fourth quarter alone. US crude rose to nearly 70 dollars a barrel last year. Rex Tillerson took over as chief executive on 1 January from Lee Raymond, who retired.
source: ExxonMobil 4Q05 investor relations data summary (Form 8-K of 30 January 2006, exhibit 99.2), https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/34088/000003408806000025/r4q05ex992.htm (read 2026-10-03); ExxonMobil press release of 31 January 2005 (2004 profit), https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/34088/000003408805000026/r013105ex991.htm (read 2026-10-03); https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/DCOILWTICO (read 2026-10-03); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rex_Tillerson (read 2026-10-03); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lee_Raymond (read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: Rex Tillerson of Exxon Mobil talking with Vice President Dick Cheney in the White House, June 2007
imageCredit: public domain, White House (Office of Management and Administration), via DPLA

headline: Disney buys Pixar for 7.4 billion dollars
text: On 24 January Disney agreed to buy Pixar, the computer animation studio behind Toy Story and Finding Nemo, for about 7.4 billion dollars in Disney shares. Pixar's chief executive Steve Jobs will join Disney's board.
imageCaption: Pixar Animation Studios, Emeryville, California ;;

headline: Amazon starts renting out storage over the internet
text: On 14 March Amazon launched S3, a service that stores other companies' data on Amazon's computers for a fee, under the name Amazon Web Services.
imageCaption: Jeff Bezos, founder of Amazon.com

headline: China's hunger drives copper to a record
text: Copper reached about $9,000 a tonne in May, up from about $1,600 in 1999. China's factories and building sites are swallowing metals, oil and iron ore; oil passed $60 a barrel last August.
imageCaption: Refined copper cathodes

headline: Hostile bid for Falconbridge as copper hits records
text: On 18 May Xstrata launched a hostile all-cash bid of C$52.50 a share for the 80% of Falconbridge it does not own, challenging an agreed takeover by the Canadian nickel miner Inco. Copper averaged a record $8,046 a tonne in May, up from $4,734 in January, and nickel and zinc are also at records.
source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Falconbridge_Ltd.; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000889211/000104746906010982/a2172709zsc14d1fa.htm; World Bank Pink Sheet monthly averages (all read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: A Boeing 737 in Xstrata Nickel colours, flown for Falconbridge's nickel operations in Canada

headline: Buffett to give most of his fortune to the Gates Foundation
text: Warren Buffett announced in June that he will give away 85% of his Berkshire shares to five foundations in yearly gifts starting in July, the largest share going to the Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation. It is the largest charitable pledge in history.
imageCaption: Warren Buffett greets shareholders at the Berkshire Hathaway annual meeting, Omaha, April 2005

headline: Winterthur sold to AXA
text: On 14 June Credit Suisse agreed to sell the Winterthur insurance group to the French insurer AXA. The bank wants to concentrate on private banking, investment banking and asset management as one integrated bank.
imageCaption: A Winterthur Insurance building, Winterthur, Switzerland

headline: World Cup in Germany: the Swiss go out without conceding a goal
text: At the World Cup in Germany, Switzerland drew 0-0 with France, beat Togo and South Korea 2-0 each and won its group. In the round of 16 on 26 June it lost to Ukraine on penalties after a 0-0 draw, missing all three of its penalties. Switzerland is the first team ever to leave a World Cup without conceding a goal.
imageCaption: Supporters in Cologne on the day of Ukraine v Switzerland, World Cup round of 16, 26 June 2006

headline: Gates will step back from Microsoft
text: On 15 June Bill Gates announced that over two years he will leave his day-to-day role at Microsoft, by July 2008. He remains chairman.
imageCaption: Bill Gates, April 2006
imageCredit: CC BY-SA 2.0, photo: Filipe Fortes from New York, United States

headline: New chief and a networks merger with Siemens
text: On 1 June Olli-Pekka Kallasvuo succeeded Jorma Ollila as chief executive; Ollila stays as chairman. On 19 June Nokia and Siemens agreed to merge most of their network equipment businesses into a 50-50 venture, Nokia Siemens Networks, with 20 billion dollars of sales last year.
imageCaption: Olli-Pekka Kallasvuo, Nokia's new chief executive, with India's prime minister Manmohan Singh, New Delhi

headline: Seventeenth hike in a row; gold falls back from a 26-year high
text: On 29 June the Fed raised its rate target to 5.25 percent, its seventeenth quarter-point increase since June 2004, under Ben Bernanke, chairman since 1 February. Gold, which averaged 675 dollars in May, its highest since January 1980, fell back to an average of 596 dollars in June, 12 percent less. Inflation was 4.2 percent in May.
imageCaption: Ben Bernanke is sworn in as Federal Reserve chairman, Washington, February 2006
imageCredit: public domain, photo: White House photo by Kimberlee Hewitt

headline: Siemens and Nokia merge their network businesses
text: On 19 June Siemens and Nokia agreed to combine most of their telecom equipment businesses in a 50-50 venture, Nokia Siemens Networks, with 20 billion dollars of sales last year. Up to 9,000 jobs are expected to go. Siemens shares jumped 8.3% on the day.
imageCaption: Nokia Siemens Networks office at Karaportti, Espoo, Finland
imageCredit: CC BY-SA 3.0, photo: Original uploader was Yordan Georgiev at bg.wikipedia

headline: Wal-Mart gives up on Germany
text: On 28 July Wal-Mart said it will sell its 85 German stores to the rival Metro and leave the country, taking a loss of about one billion dollars. Vice chairman Mike Duke said it had become clear that Wal-Mart could not reach the scale and results it wanted there.
source: https://www.forbes.com/2006/07/28/walmart-germany-metro-cx_po_0728walmart.html (search result summary read 2026-10-03); https://www.cbsnews.com/news/wal-marts-german-flop/ (search result summary read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: Wertkauf logo, the German chain Wal-Mart bought in 1997

headline: Xstrata wins Falconbridge
text: After raising its offer to C$62.50 a share in cash, Xstrata took up 257.7 million Falconbridge shares on 14 August and now owns about 92% of the company; Inco's competing bid lapsed in July. The bid values Falconbridge at more than C$20bn; it adds Sudbury nickel and large copper interests, and the business will become Xstrata Nickel, based in Toronto.
imageCaption: Xstrata's Nikkelverk nickel refinery, Kristiansand, Norway

headline: Judge finds the tobacco companies guilty of racketeering
text: On 17 August federal judge Gladys Kessler ruled in a 1,683-page opinion that Philip Morris and the other big tobacco companies violated the racketeering (RICO) law by conspiring for decades to deny the health risks and addictiveness of smoking and by marketing to children. She ordered them to stop using terms like 'light' and 'low tar' and to publish corrective statements, but imposed no damages. Earlier this year the Florida Supreme Court decertified the Engle class, ending the 145 billion dollar award for good, but let individual smokers rely on the jury's findings.
imageCaption: Judge Gladys Kessler, who decided the racketeering case against the tobacco companies
imageCredit: public domain, photo: United States Government

headline: Intel cuts 10,500 jobs after losing ground to AMD
text: Intel will eliminate 10,500 jobs, about a tenth of its workforce, through layoffs, attrition and the sale of business groups, and trim about 5 billion dollars of costs over two years. It has lost market share to AMD, whose Opteron and Athlon 64 chips have been ahead since 2003. Chief executive Paul Otellini compared the overhaul to the exit from memory chips in the 1980s.
imageCaption: Intel executives Paul Otellini, Craig Barrett and Sean Maloney, 2006
imageCredit: CC BY-SA 2.0, photo: Intel Free Press

headline: McDonald's lets go of Chipotle and raises its dividend 50%
text: McDonald's raised its annual dividend by nearly 50% to 1 dollar a share in late September, four times the level of 2002, and offered its shareholders Chipotle shares in exchange for McDonald's shares; in October it fully divested its majority stake in the Mexican grill chain. It is concentrating on the McDonald's brand and returning cash to shareholders.
imageCaption: A Chipotle Mexican Grill restaurant

headline: Police raid Siemens in a bribery investigation
text: On 15 November more than 200 police officers searched Siemens offices across Germany, looking for evidence of bribery. Prosecutors in Italy, Liechtenstein and Switzerland are also investigating, and the telecom unit is at the centre of the inquiry.
imageCaption: Siemens headquarters on Wittelsbacherplatz, Munich

headline: Third record year in a row: $4 billion profit
text: Lehman Brothers earned a record $4.0 billion in the year to November 2006, up 23%, or $6.81 a share, its third consecutive year of record revenues and profits, with a pre-tax margin of 33.6%. Institutional Investor magazine named Richard Fuld the top chief executive among brokers and asset managers.
imageCaption: Lehman Brothers' headquarters on Seventh Avenue, New York, June 2006

headline: First UN sanctions on Iran over enrichment
text: On 23 December the UN Security Council voted 15 to 0 for Resolution 1737, which bans the supply of nuclear technology to Iran and freezes the assets of people and companies tied to its enrichment programme until Iran suspends enrichment. Iran's UN ambassador said 'a nation is being punished for exercising its inalienable rights'.
imageCaption: The UN Security Council in session, December 2006
